description: Platform applicability tags for checklist items. An item listed here is evaluated only on the platforms in 'applies_to' and only when the instance satisfies every gate present. Items absent from this file apply everywhere. Tag out ONLY where the feature does not exist on the platform - never where responsibility merely shifts to the provider, and never where only the evidence surface moves (see docs/not-applicable-handling.md sections 4, 6.4 and 6.5).

gates.applies_to: Deployment platform. SqlServer covers on-premises and SQL Server on an Azure VM.
gates.min_edition: SqlServer only, ignored on Azure. Rank: Express (incl. LocalDB) < Web < Standard < BusinessIntelligence < Enterprise. Developer and Evaluation rank as Enterprise.
gates.min_version: SqlServer only, ignored on Azure. Release year compared against SERVERPROPERTY('ProductMajorVersion').
gates.min_tier: Azure only, ignored on SqlServer. BusinessCritical is satisfied by Azure SQL Database Premium / Business Critical / Hyperscale and by Managed Instance Business Critical.

1.1.4.reason: vCore/DTU and Business Critical/General Purpose are Azure service-tier constructs. On-premises compute sizing is covered generically by 12.1.1.

1.3.3.reason: Readable secondary replicas require Enterprise edition on SQL Server, and Premium / Business Critical / Hyperscale on Azure SQL.

1.3.7.reason: AG listeners and FCI virtual network names are SQL Server constructs. CREATE AVAILABILITY GROUP is unsupported on Managed Instance and Azure SQL Database uses failover-group endpoints.

1.3.8.reason: MultiSubnetFailover applies to multi-subnet availability groups, which cannot be user-managed on either Azure SQL platform.

1.3.9.reason: Client aliases and DNS repointing on failover are on-premises concerns; Azure SQL exposes no equivalent alias surface.

1.3.10.reason: Node-level parity (instance configuration, trace flags, MAXDOP, Agent jobs) presumes user-visible cluster nodes. Trace flags are unsupported on Azure SQL Database and limited to a fixed global set on Managed Instance.

4.4.3.reason: Azure SQL Database supports the primary filegroup only.

4.4.5.reason: Managed Instance fixes tempdb at 12 data files and the structure cannot be changed; Azure SQL Database exposes no tempdb file configuration.

4.4.6.reason: Azure SQL Database manages data and log file growth as part of the service; autogrowth is not user-configurable.

6.2.1.reason: Transparent Data Encryption reached Standard edition only in SQL Server 2019; on 2016 and 2017 it is Enterprise-only. It is enabled by default on both Azure SQL platforms.

6.2.7.reason: Backup encryption is unavailable on SQL Server Express. Azure SQL backups are encrypted automatically by the service.

6.3.3.reason: Public network access is an Azure resource-level setting with no on-premises equivalent.

6.3.4.reason: Broad inbound exposure is an Azure control-plane concern: IP firewall rules on Azure SQL Database, and a public endpoint with an over-permissive network security group on Managed Instance. Evidence is in ARM, not T-SQL.

6.4.3.reason: Managed identity for service-to-service authentication requires SQL Server 2022 with Azure Arc; earlier releases have no equivalent. Fully available on both Azure SQL platforms.

8.1.4.reason: Azure SQL Database supports neither linked servers nor cross-database three-part-name queries, so both halves of this control are unavailable.

9.1.7.reason: Both Azure SQL Database and Managed Instance run FULL recovery exclusively; SIMPLE and BULK_LOGGED are unavailable and RECOVERY cannot be altered.

9.2.10.reason: Windows Server Failover Clustering is not supported on either Azure SQL platform, so no quorum model exists.

9.2.11.reason: Backup replica preference presumes user-managed availability replicas, which Azure SQL does not expose.

9.2.12.reason: No AG listener or client alias artifact exists on Azure SQL; failover groups provide the equivalent endpoint and are covered by 9.2.7.

9.3.1.reason: Azure SQL Database has no SQL Server Agent to schedule integrity checks and consistency is verified by the platform.

9.3.2.reason: PAGE_VERIFY is fixed at CHECKSUM and listed as unmodifiable on Managed Instance; it is not exposed on Azure SQL Database.

12.1.2.reason: DTU and vCore are Azure metering constructs; on-premises resource profiling is covered by 12.2.2.

12.1.3.reason: Elastic pools exist only on Azure SQL Database. Managed Instance uses instance pools, a different construct.

12.1.4.reason: The serverless auto-scaling tier exists only on Azure SQL Database; Managed Instance requires reserved compute.

14.3.6.reason: Isolating reporting onto a read replica requires Enterprise edition on SQL Server, and Premium / Business Critical / Hyperscale on Azure SQL. Same constraint as 1.3.3.

14.4.1.reason: Managed Instance fixes tempdb at 12 data files and the structure cannot be changed; Azure SQL Database exposes no tempdb file configuration.

14.4.3.reason: Resource Governor requires Enterprise edition on SQL Server and is unsupported on Azure SQL Database. It is supported on Managed Instance.
